ACCEPT — for the stated separated-negative-source classUnder the established source-fusion model, geometric receiver catalogue, original-owner ledger, and marked-side injection, the note proves
$$\boxed{\sigma\ge |N-B|+2R.}$$
I find no missing geometric step in the forced-filling argument and no double spending in the reservation or final counting.This acceptance covers complete feasible fusions of the specified  $U$  modules, negative rotors, and the permitted  $2P1T$ -only zero rotors, subject to physical receiver-tile separation between distinct negative sources. It is acceptance of the written mathematical deduction from the granted inputs. It does not certify the reported computations or a compiled arbitrary-source geometric adapter.There are two wording corrections worth making in §3: a  $1P2T$  profile does have a diagonal blank, and the reservation does not require the stronger assertion that all marked sides have distinct donor tiles. Neither correction changes the theorem or requires a new hypothesis.1. Forced filling is validThe essential feasibility fact is that an original selection which survives in  $T$  cannot have its retained endpoint anchor and a second occupied neighbor. In the usual formulation, this uses both independence of  $T$  and the prohibition on two endpoint neighbors of a surviving selection. I use this as part of the granted source-fusion model.Also, every original selection remains occupied: from
$$P=\bigcup_i P_i,\qquad T=\Bigl(\bigcup_i T_i\Bigr)\setminus P,$$
an original selected site either remains in  $T$  or belongs to the fixed final endpoint union  $P$ .These are necessary consequences of final feasibility. The argument does not assume that endpoints can be added freely when a filling obligation appears.Negative  $1P1T$ Normalize the negative endpoint to  $0$ , its original selection to  $1$ , and an irregular-event endpoint to  $2$ . Thus  $0,2\in P$ , and  $1$  remains occupied.By (H), the original owner of endpoint  $2$  is nonnegative. Its profile is therefore GOOD.Foreign  $1P2T$ . Its original selections are  $0$  and  $3$ , so  $3$  remains occupied. If  $1$  remained selected, it would have its anchor  $0$  and the additional occupied neighbor  $3$ , contrary to feasibility. Hence  $1\in P$ . Site  $3$ , now adjacent to the two distinct endpoints  $1,2$ , likewise cannot remain selected. Thus  $3\in P$ .Foreign  $2P1T$ . Connectedness puts its second endpoint at  $0$  or  $3$ . Original endpoint disjointness excludes  $0$ , so  $3\in P$ . The original selection at  $1$  then has endpoint neighbors  $0,3$ , forcing  $1\in P$ .Foreign  $4P0T$ . This would include the already owned negative endpoint  $0$ , violating original endpoint disjointness.Consequently all four corners belong to  $P$ .The first case genuinely uses the restriction on a second occupied neighbor: at its first forcing step, site  $3$  is known to be occupied but is not yet known to be an endpoint. The granted feasibility rule supplies exactly that step.Negative  $2P0T$ Here the actual geometric catalogue matters: the two endpoints of a bar profile are adjacent. Normalize them to  $0,1$ , with the event endpoint at  $2$ .A foreign  $1P2T$  profile at  $2$  makes site  $3$  occupied. Since  $3$  is adjacent to endpoints  $1,2$ , it must belong to  $P$ .A foreign  $2P1T$  profile at  $2$  has its other endpoint at  $0$  or  $3$ . Disjointness excludes  $0$ , so it lies at  $3$ .A foreign  $4P0T$  profile is impossible by endpoint disjointness.Again all four corners belong to  $P$ .Thus the local implication needed later is established:
$$K_{\mathrm{irregular}}(Q)>0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
Q\text{ is endpoint-full}.$$
Moreover, this is a new mixed full tile, which should be stated explicitly before spending its credit. It contains endpoints from the negative owner and a foreign owner. No original  $4P0T$  owner could have occupied it alongside the negative endpoint. Therefore the indicator in the definition of  $c_Q$  is indeed one.No feasibility assumption about a two-source subunion was used.2. The leftover credit is correctly bounded tile by tileFix an irregular-event tile  $Q$ . Its unique negative owner has one or two original endpoints there. Every other endpoint owner in  $Q$  is GOOD, by (H) and the restriction on zero rotors.The regular-event count is bounded by the actual local geometry:A  $1P2T$  owner has both intratile neighbors of its endpoint selected originally. Its remaining blank is diagonal to that endpoint, so it supplies no regular-event tail.A connected  $2P1T$  owner has one original blank, adjacent to exactly one of its endpoints. It supplies at most one regular event.At most one such two-endpoint owner fits in the three or two corners left by the negative owner.A  $4P0T$  owner cannot coexist with the negative endpoint.Hence
$$K_{\mathrm{regular}}(Q)\le1.$$
Because  $Q$  is new mixed full,
$$c_Q=2-K_{\mathrm{regular}}(Q)\ge1.$$
This is the correct leftover credit: regular events have already been deducted in the definition of  $c_Q$ . The proof spends only what remains.For the negative profiles themselves:In a  $1P1T$  tile, the endpoint has one selected intratile neighbor and one blank intratile neighbor. There is at most one irregular tail.In an adjacent  $2P0T$  tile, the two blank corners are each adjacent to exactly one of the negative endpoints. There are at most two irregular tails.Therefore
$$K_{\mathrm{irregular}}(Q)\le c_Q$$
for a negative  $1P1T$  tile, and
$$K_{\mathrm{irregular}}(Q)\le c_Q+1$$
for a negative  $2P0T$  tile. The zero-event cases follow from  $c_Q\ge0$ .The allowance of negative  $3P0T$  profiles elsewhere causes no problem here: under (H), such a profile cannot belong to a second negative owner in the irregular-event tile being charged. Its regular events remain covered by the established regular-tile inequality.3. The corner reservation and irregular excess are mutually exclusiveThe cleanest formulation of the reservation is entirely tilewise. Define
$$a_Q=
\#\{\text{marked sides assigned to phase-(1,1) upper corners in }Q\},$$
and
$$\ell_Q=
\mathbf 1_{\{Q\text{ is a row-shifted negative }2P0T
\text{ bar tile}\}}.$$
The supplied inputs imply
$$a_Q\in\{0,1\},\qquad a_Q\le\ell_Q.$$
Here is the complete capacity argument:An endpoint receives at most one assignment, by endpoint injection.The two phase- $(1,1)$  upper corners of one  $U$  lie in different bar tiles.Upper corners of different negative sources cannot lie in the same receiver tile, by (H).Thus at most one  $A$ -assignment can use a given bar tile. No general injection from marked sides to physical donor tiles is needed.Now consider the two cases.A tile with  $a_Q=1$ The established gate implication leaves the adjacent old intratile blank unoccupied. Hence  $Q$  is not full. The forced-filling implication proved above gives
$$K_{\mathrm{irregular}}(Q)=0.$$
In fact, the regular-tile bound also gives
$$0\le K_{\mathrm{regular}}(Q)
\le 2\mathbf 1_{\{Q\text{ is new mixed full}\}}=0,$$
so  $c_Q=0$ . Therefore
$$K_{\mathrm{irregular}}(Q)+a_Q
=1
=c_Q+\ell_Q.$$
The corner assignment consumes precisely the one bar reservation. There is no irregular-event debit in that tile.A tile with  $a_Q=0$ The local payment inequalities give
$$K_{\mathrm{irregular}}(Q)\le c_Q+\ell_Q.$$
This also covers tiles without an irregular event, since  $c_Q\ge0$ .Combining the cases yields the single inequality
$$\boxed{
K_{\mathrm{irregular}}(Q)+a_Q\le c_Q+\ell_Q
}
\qquad\text{for every physical tile }Q.$$
By the catalogue and (H), the row-shifted bar tiles counted in  $L$  are distinct physical reservation tiles. Thus
$$\sum_Q\ell_Q=L,\qquad \sum_Qa_Q=A,$$
and summation gives exactly
$$\boxed{K_{\mathrm{irregular}}+A\le C+L.}$$
This establishes the claimed single-use accounting. Each  $c_Q$  stays in its own tile. Each bar unit pays either an upper-corner assignment or the possible irregular-event excess. Those uses cannot occur together.The argument requires only the established conditional gate implication. It does not require a physical example realizing an upper-corner assignment, and makes no existence or sharpness claim about that branch.4. Both bounds on  $E$  follow from the stated injectionBecause  $A$  counts a subset of the  $G$  marked-side assignments,
$$E=G-A$$
is exactly the number of remaining assignments.After removing phase- $(1,1)$  upper-corner assignments, the boundary catalogue leaves:the two phase- $(0,1)$  upper corners of a negative  $U$ ; orthe two terminal tips of a row-shifted negative  $U$ .Thus each negative  $U$  offers at most two endpoints of the remaining types. No rotor endpoint can receive an assignment. Global endpoint injectivity therefore gives
$$E\le2B.$$
Independently, every positive  $U$  has only two canonical sides, so
$$E\le G\le2N.$$
These are simultaneous upper bounds on the same set of assignments:
$$\boxed{E\le\min(2N,2B)=2\min(N,B).}$$
There is no assumption that the candidate endpoints are occupied by assignments, no surjectivity requirement, and no need for  $N$  and  $B$  to be comparable. Nor are the two bounds being spent as separate resources: they are simply two caps on the one remaining debit  $E$ .5. The source-mass cancellation and conclusion are exactLet  $B_{01}$  count phase- $(0,1)$  negative  $U$  sources. The supplied source masses give
$$S
=
B_{01}
+\sum_{\text{row-shifted negative }U}(w_i-1)
+2R.$$
Since
$$w_i-1=(w_i-2)+1,$$
and  $B$  counts both phase- $(0,1)$  and row-shifted negative  $U$  sources,
$$\boxed{S=L+B+2R.}$$
Using  $G=A+E$  in the established ledger,
$$\begin{aligned}
\sigma
&\ge N+S+C-K_{\mathrm{irregular}}-A-E\\
&\ge N+S-L-E\\
&=N+B+2R-E\\
&\ge N+B+2R-2\min(N,B)\\
&=|N-B|+2R.
\end{aligned}$$
This explains exactly why widths disappear: their contribution to the negative source mass supplies the  $L$  bar reservations and cancels them. Leg heights enter neither the remaining assignment count nor this accounting.The edge cases  $N=0$ ,  $B=0$ , and  $N=B$  need no separate hypothesis. With exactly one negative  $U$  and no negative rotors, (H) is automatic, so the stated consequence with arbitrarily many positive  $U$  modules and permitted zero rotors follows.6. Precise wording correctionsI would make the following edits without changing the theorem’s status.First, correct this sentence in §3:“An owner with a singleton  $1P2T$  profile has no original intratile blank…”A  $1P2T$  tile has one blank. Replace it with:“An owner with a singleton  $1P2T$  profile has no original intratile blank adjacent to its endpoint: its only blank is diagonal. It therefore contributes no regular event.”Second, replace the broad donor-tile assertion in the reservation paragraph.The statement“distinct marked sides have distinct original donor tiles”is stronger than the endpoint injection expressly supplied in the question. The theorem does not need it. Use:“A bar tile receives at most one  $A$ -assignment: endpoint injection prevents reuse of a corner, the two upper corners of one phase- $(1,1)$   $U$  lie in distinct bar tiles, and (H) separates corners belonging to different negative sources.”Also, adding “new mixed” to the conclusion of §2 makes the subsequent use of  $c_Q$  immediate.Finally, the  $3P0T$  obstruction in §5 is consistent with this audit. A local negative profile  $P=\{0\}, T=\{1\}$ , together with a foreign  $3P0T$  profile on  $\{1,2,3\}$ , produces one irregular tail and two regular tails into the old blank  $0$ , giving  $c_Q=0$ . This demonstrates failure of the local payment rule when that foreign profile is allowed. As the note correctly states, it does not supply a complete feasible counterexample to the final inequality.The accepted result is therefore the stated compensation theorem under (H) and the permitted source catalogue, with no additional density, contact-graph, pair-feasibility, or degree assumption.
